The board sounded out Arm's Rene Haas as Reuters reported Huang misled Nvidia's own general counsel.

stories.title: The FAA orders a rare nationwide ground stop for all US departures on 13 Nov after communication failures hit its Air Route Traffic Control Centers; DHS says there is no sign of an attack, CBS sources blame an update to ATC's private communications network that rebooted and crashed it, and FlightAware counts thousands of cancellations and 10,000+ delays
stories.h: FAA halts all US departures as air traffic control communications fail nationwide
stories.sub: The third nationwide ground stop in FAA history; DHS sees no attack, and early reporting points to a bad network update.
stories.ticker: FAA grounds all US departures after air traffic control communications fail
stories.body:
The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports on Friday afternoon, citing communication issues affecting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, the 22 centres that handle planes above 18,000 feet. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage with no indication of a "nefarious" act. Multiple sources told CBS News an update to the private network that links the air traffic control system made it reboot and crash. By the evening FlightAware counted more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000+ delays (ABC); some flights were later allowed to depart as centres recovered. Ars Technica says it is only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history. The contractor behind the FAA's new AI congestion tool, and Microsoft, both said they were not the cause (Business Insider).

So what: a single network change grounded the world's busiest airspace for hours, a day after a Microsoft 365 outage traced to a network capacity upgrade. Banks and insurers should expect claims, travel-cover and business-interruption questions, and every operations team should re-read its own change-control rules for shared networks.
stories.chip: Checked on the FAA's own statement; cause, counts and quotes from ABC News, Ars Technica and Business Insider
src: FAA: Statement on Nationwide Ground Stop
Hacker News: FAA issues national ground stop (1,206 points)
stories.brief:
The FAA's statement is brief and marked preliminary: a nationwide ground stop for all US airports following communication issues at multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, with technicians investigating. Everything about the cause comes from reporting. CBS News, citing multiple sources, says an update to the private communications network connecting the air traffic control system caused it to reboot and crash. Bloomberg reports the FBI is looking at whether a bad software update was responsible. DHS says there is no sign of an attack.

The impact landed on a Friday evening: thousands of cancellations, college sports teams stranded, Canadian airports bracing for knock-on delays. The FAA said some flights could depart as en-route centres recovered, but no all-clear had been given at the time of writing.
facts: Nationwide ground stop for all US departures
Communication issues at multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers
Network update made the ATC communications system reboot and crash (CBS sources)
stories.impactWho: Airlines, travellers and freight; insurers handling travel and business-interruption claims; anyone running critical systems on a shared network.
stories.short: The FAA halted all US departures on Friday after communication failures hit its en-route air traffic control centres. DHS says there is no sign of an attack; CBS sources say an update to ATC's private network made it reboot and crash. Thousands of flights were cancelled and more than 10,000 delayed. The full cause is not yet confirmed.

stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, letting its 'dots' agents complete purchases with US Pro users' Visa, Mastercard and Amex cards via network tokens (the agent never sees the card number), with each purchase approved by Face ID or fingerprint; OpenAI takes no transaction cut at launch and plans spending limits and category rules
stories.h: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's agents pay with your card, without seeing it
stories.ticker: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet: agents buy with Visa, Mastercard, Amex tokens
stories.body:
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its dots agents choose and complete purchases. It starts with a limited number of US ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18+ with a US-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express card. The agent pays with a payment token rather than the card number, users review the items, total and card first, and every purchase is approved with Face ID or a fingerprint, keeping existing card rewards and protections. OpenAI plans spending limits and rules by category or time window so agents can be pre-approved; CNBC reports OpenAI is not taking a share of transaction revenue at launch. OpenAI warns some sites and fraud systems will still block agent purchases.

So what: this is the card networks' tokenised agent-payment rails going live inside the biggest consumer AI app. Issuers need to decide how their fraud models treat agent-initiated, biometrically approved transactions, who is liable when an agent buys the wrong thing, and how disputes will work.
stories.chip: Checked on TechCrunch's report of the launch; OpenAI's own post blocked automated access (403)
stories.short: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, letting its dots agents buy things for a limited group of US Pro users with Visa, Mastercard or Amex cards. Agents pay with a network token, never the card number, and each purchase needs Face ID or a fingerprint. OpenAI takes no transaction cut at launch and plans spending limits and category rules.

stat.label: card networks at launch: Visa, Mastercard, Amex

stories.title: The 10-year Treasury yield reaches 5.17% on 13 Nov, its highest since October, as traders brace for a December Fed hike; the Nasdaq falls about 0.9% and the S&P 500 0.4% as Nvidia's slide deepens, the Dow edges up, and bitcoin drops below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months
stories.h: Ten-year yield hits 5.17% as December hike bets grow; bitcoin breaks $70,000
stories.ticker: US 10-year yield touches 5.17%; Nasdaq -0.9%; bitcoin below $70k
stories.body:
The 10-year Treasury yield reached as high as 5.17% on Friday, its highest since October, as traders braced for a December rate hike (Yahoo Finance); closing reports put it around 5.13%. The Nasdaq fell about 0.9% and the S&P 500 0.4% as Nvidia's slide deepened after its CEO's exit, while the Dow rose slightly. Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months; Coinbase Institutional says rate expectations, not the Binance theft, drove the drop.

So what: a 5%+ 10-year resets mortgage, corporate-bond and bank funding costs, and puts pressure on bond portfolios held at fair value. With a December hike now the base case for many traders, treasury desks should stress-test deposit costs and unrealised losses again.
stories.chip: Checked on Yahoo Finance's markets live page; closing levels also reported by CNBC
src: Yahoo Finance: stock market today, 13 Nov
Crypto Briefing: Coinbase Institutional on bitcoin
stories.short: The US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17% on Friday, its highest since October, as traders priced a December Fed hike. The Nasdaq fell about 0.9% as Nvidia's slide deepened, the Dow edged up, and bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months. Exact closing yields vary by source, around 5.13%.

stories.title: The White House says President Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together on 19 Nov in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit, an unprecedented three-way meeting of the biggest nuclear powers; nuclear arms reduction and the Iran war are on the agenda, Ukraine largely off it, and US officials expect no agreement
stories.h: Trump, Xi and Putin to meet together in Shenzhen on 19 November
stories.ticker: Trump, Xi and Putin plan joint meeting at APEC in Shenzhen on 19 Nov
stories.body:
The leaders of the US, China and Russia plan to meet on Thursday 19 November on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, the White House says, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's largest nuclear powers. AP reports nuclear arms reduction will be discussed and Trump is expected to raise the Iran war, while a US official said he will steer away from Ukraine. Analysts expect symbolism over substance and US officials do not expect an agreement.

So what: the meeting lands the same week as Nvidia's leadership crisis and pending US chip curbs, so any word on export controls or AI dialogue will move chip and China-exposed stocks. Expect volatility in oil if Iran comes up.
stories.chip: Checked on The Manila Times (AP); Bloomberg and the Washington Post report the same
stories.short: The White House says Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together on 19 November in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC: the first such three-way meeting. Nuclear arms reduction and the Iran war are expected topics; Ukraine largely is not. US officials say they do not expect an agreement.

stories.title: The RBI grants Paytm Payments Services (PPSL), a One 97 Communications subsidiary, in-principle authorisation to issue prepaid payment instruments including wallets, more than two years after curbs on Paytm Payments Bank; PPSL must pass a system and cybersecurity audit within six months before final authorisation, and Paytm shares hit a record
stories.h: RBI clears Paytm to restart wallets through a new subsidiary, in principle
stories.ticker: RBI gives Paytm's PPSL in-principle nod for wallets; shares at record high
stories.body:
The Reserve Bank of India has granted Paytm Payments Services Ltd (PPSL), a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, in-principle authorisation to issue and operate prepaid payment instruments, including wallets. PPSL must complete a system and cybersecurity audit within six months or the approval lapses, and can issue wallets only after final authorisation. Paytm's old wallet ran through Paytm Payments Bank, which the RBI barred from new customers in 2022 and from new deposits in 2024; this approval is for a separate entity. Paytm shares hit a record high.

So what: the RBI is letting a once-sanctioned group back into wallets through a cleaner structure, which tells fintechs how to rebuild after enforcement. Banks competing for UPI and wallet users should expect Paytm to push hard once final approval comes.
stories.chip: Checked on Business Standard and Entrackr, both citing the RBI letter of 13 Nov
stories.short: The RBI has given Paytm Payments Services, a subsidiary of Paytm's parent, in-principle approval to issue wallets and other prepaid instruments, years after its payments bank was shut down. It must pass a system and cybersecurity audit within six months before it can launch. Paytm shares hit a record high.

stat.label: to pass the RBI audit or the nod lapses

stories.title: SEBI approves Razorpay's IPO; the payments company aims to raise about Rs 5,000-6,000 crore to grow its financial services platform, and Sembcorp Green Infra also gets the nod for a Rs 3,750 crore fresh issue
stories.h: SEBI approves Razorpay's IPO, which could raise up to Rs 6,000 crore
stories.ticker: SEBI approves Razorpay IPO; Rs 5,000-6,000 crore target
stories.body:
India's market regulator SEBI has approved the IPO of payments company Razorpay, which aims to raise about Rs 5,000-6,000 crore (roughly $590-710M) to expand its financial services platform, the Economic Times reports. Renewable power producer Sembcorp Green Infra also received approval for a Rs 3,750 crore fresh issue.

So what: with Paytm back in wallets and Razorpay heading to market, India's payment infrastructure firms are moving from private funding to public scrutiny. Public filings will give banks a detailed look at merchant-acquiring margins and fraud costs.
stories.chip: Checked on the Economic Times; YourStory reports the same
stories.short: SEBI has approved Razorpay's IPO. The Indian payments company aims to raise about Rs 5,000-6,000 crore, roughly $590-710 million, to grow its financial services platform, the Economic Times reports. Sembcorp Green Infra also won approval. Timing and valuation have not been announced.

stories.title: President Trump nominates four commissioners: Republican Steven Levine to replace crypto advocate Hester Peirce at the SEC and Democrat Kristin Johnson (ex-CFTC) for Caroline Crenshaw's seat, plus Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both Clarity Act veterans, at the CFTC, where chairman Mike Selig is the only member
stories.h: Trump names four SEC and CFTC picks, including Hester Peirce's successor
stories.ticker: Trump nominates Levine for Peirce's SEC seat; two CFTC picks
stories.body:
The White House nominated Steven Levine (R) for the SEC seat of Hester Peirce, who led the agency's crypto task force, and former CFTC commissioner Kristin Johnson (D) for Caroline Crenshaw's seat. At the CFTC, where chairman Mike Selig is the sole commissioner, it nominated Nathan Anonick (R) and Matthew Rowland (D), both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. Levine's views on crypto are less publicly known; Johnson has pushed for stronger customer protection. Republicans have only a short lame-duck window before Democrats take the Senate in January.

So what: the agencies writing US crypto and prediction-market rules have been running with skeleton commissions. Whether these nominees are confirmed this year decides how fast stablecoin, custody and event-contract rules move in 2027.
stories.chip: Checked on Cointelegraph; MLQ and others report the same four names
stories.short: Trump nominated Steven Levine to replace crypto advocate Hester Peirce at the SEC, and former CFTC commissioner Kristin Johnson for a second SEC seat. Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland, both Clarity Act veterans, were named to the CFTC, which has only its chairman. Confirmation must come before Democrats take the Senate in January.

stories.title: Trezor confirms hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by former Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that copy recovery phrases from the screen and send them over a cellular link; firmware 2.13.1 (11 Nov) blocks capture, affected owners must move funds to a new seed, and Trezor has cut its reseller network by about 80%
stories.h: Trezor finds phrase-stealing implants in three hardware wallets from one reseller
stories.ticker: Trezor confirms implants in 3 Safe 5 wallets; firmware 2.13.1 blocks them
stories.body:
Hardware-wallet maker Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants that capture recovery phrases and passphrases and send them over cellular networks. The firmware and secure chip were not altered. Firmware 2.13.1, released 11 November, stops the implants it found from capturing anything, but cannot recall phrases already sent, so owners should move funds to a wallet with a new seed. Implants were earlier found in Ledger devices sold by the same reseller. Trezor has cut its reseller network by about 80%.

So what: hardware supply chains are now an attack path for self-custody. Banks building crypto custody should buy devices only from manufacturers or audited channels and treat any third-party reseller as untrusted.
stories.chip: Checked on BleepingComputer, which quotes Trezor's statement
stories.short: Trezor confirmed malicious hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by reseller CryptoBilis; they send recovery phrases out over a cellular link. Firmware 2.13.1 blocks the implants it found, but owners must move funds to a new seed. Trezor has cut its reseller network by about 80%. No losses have been reported, Trezor says.

stories.title: The FBI issues a flash alert that Artex, an AI penetration-testing platform, is being used by attackers to automate reconnaissance and data theft at 'machine speed', mostly driven by Chinese models led by DeepSeek Flash; Censys counts 1,600+ exposed Artex consoles
stories.h: FBI warns attackers are running the Artex AI hacking tool at machine speed
stories.ticker: FBI flash alert: Artex AI tool automating cyberattacks; 1,600+ exposed consoles
stories.body:
An FBI flash alert says Artex, a penetration-testing platform that turns plain-language goals into attack commands, is being used by threat actors for reconnaissance and data exfiltration at machine speed. The FBI says attacker-run Artex instances mostly use Chinese models, with DeepSeek Flash models dominating for their cost and lack of guardrails when framed as pen testing, alongside Claude, GPT and others. Censys has found 1,600+ publicly exposed Artex consoles; archived copies and a commercial version keep it available.

So what: this moves AI-run intrusion from research to an official law-enforcement warning. Security teams should expect faster, wider scanning and shorter dwell times, and should block or monitor known Artex infrastructure.
stories.chip: Checked on The Record's report of the FBI alert
stories.short: An FBI flash alert says attackers are using Artex, an AI penetration-testing platform, to automate reconnaissance and data theft at machine speed. Attacker-run instances mostly use Chinese models, led by DeepSeek Flash, because they are cheap and lack guardrails. Censys counts more than 1,600 exposed Artex consoles.

stories.title: Perplexity open-sources Decider v1.3 (26B, built on Qwen3.8-27B) and Decider Flash v1.3 decision models under Apache 2.0, adding 'locate', which returns the matching text span with character offsets; both are free on OpenRouter for a week, making decision models open-weight days after Google's entry
stories.h: Perplexity open-sources its Decider decision models, adding a 'locate' skill
stories.ticker: Perplexity releases Decider v1.3 decision models under Apache 2.0
stories.body:
Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, decision models that return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice and scored questions rather than prose. The weights are on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0; the large model is a 26B fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B per its model card, and Flash is distilled from it. New in v1.3 is locate: describe what to find and the model returns the matching text with character offsets. CEO Aravind Srinivas says both are free on OpenRouter for a week. Perplexity reports 91.6% mean accuracy on 63 internal tasks (its own benchmark).

So what: a day after Google's Decision 1, the decision-model category now has a free, open-weight option banks can run on their own hardware for classification, routing and compliance checks. 'Locate' is directly useful for extracting clauses or fields with an audit trail.
stories.chip: Checked on the Hugging Face model card (Apache 2.0, Qwen3.8-27B base, 26B parameters)
src: Hacker News: Perplexity Decider v1.3 (92 points)
stories.short: Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, decision models that return probabilities instead of prose, as open weights under Apache 2.0. The large model is a 26B fine-tune of Qwen3.8-27B. A new 'locate' skill returns the matching text with character offsets. Its 91.6% accuracy figure is Perplexity's own test.

stories.title: OpenAI disbands its stand-alone robotics team, moving researchers into Mark Chen's core research group and applied robotics and hardware staff into Greg Brockman's Applied organisation, saying general models such as GPT-6 Astra can now run robots directly; it still targets a first humanoid demonstration in 2027
stories.h: OpenAI folds its robotics team into core research as GPT-6 Astra runs robots
stories.ticker: OpenAI disbands stand-alone robotics team; says general models can run robots
stories.body:
OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team, Fortune reports. Robotics research moves under chief research officer Mark Chen, and applied robotics and hardware staff join the Applied organisation under president Greg Brockman. OpenAI says researchers have seen surprising results connecting GPT-6 Astra directly to robots, so separate robot-specific models may not be needed, and that it still aims for a first public humanoid demonstration in 2027. It is the second time in six years OpenAI has dissolved a separate robotics team.

So what: the bet that one general model can drive robots, cars and drones is spreading. If it holds, robotics value shifts from specialised model labs to hardware, data and deployment, which matters for how investors price start-ups like Agile Robots and Figure.
stories.chip: Checked on Fortune's exclusive
stories.short: OpenAI has disbanded its separate robotics team, moving researchers into core research and hardware staff into its Applied organisation, Fortune reports. OpenAI says general models such as GPT-6 Astra can already run some robot tasks directly. It still plans a first public humanoid demonstration in 2027.

stories.title: Tesla opens Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990 plus a required $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription (first month included) and a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, with deliveries slated to start as soon as December
stories.h: Tesla puts the Cybercab on sale at $29,990 plus $299 a month
stories.ticker: Tesla Cybercab orders open at $29,990 plus $299/month autonomy subscription
stories.body:
Tesla has opened Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990, with a required $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription (first month included) and a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, Teslarati reports; InsideEVs and TeslaNorth report the same pricing. Deliveries could begin as soon as December. Until now the Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals, went only into Tesla's own robotaxi fleet.

So what: a two-seat car with no controls sold to individuals tests how insurers, lenders and regulators handle a vehicle that only drives itself. Auto lenders and insurers will need a view on the subscription dependency: the car is of little use without it.
stories.chip: Checked on Teslarati; InsideEVs and TeslaNorth carry the same price
stories.short: Tesla opened Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990, plus a required $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription and a $1,000 non-refundable deposit. Deliveries could start in December. Until now the two-seat car with no steering wheel or pedals went only into Tesla's own robotaxi fleet.

stories.title: Helsinki logician Jan von Plato used Claude to analyse his transcriptions of Kurt Gödel's 1940s shorthand workbooks; it catalogued 663 theorems Gödel proved, sketched or outlined, and in Coq about 400 verified as stated, about 200 needed repair and about 50 were false
stories.h: Claude helps surface 663 theorems hidden in Kurt Gödel's notebooks
stories.ticker: Claude catalogues 663 theorems in Gödel's notebooks; ~400 verified in Coq
stories.body:
Since 2017 Jan von Plato at the University of Helsinki has studied 16 notebooks, 1,009 pages, that Kurt Gödel wrote in the early 1940s in an obsolete German shorthand, at about a page a week. In September he gave his transcriptions to Claude, which produced a digest within days showing Gödel had proved hundreds of unknown theorems. Asked to extract every theorem Gödel proved, sketched or had an idea for, Claude found 663. Checked in the Coq proof assistant, about 400 were verified as stated, about 200 needed repair and about 50 were false, the Guardian reports. Claude did not read the shorthand; von Plato did.

So what: a good example of AI as a research accelerant on archives too large for a human: the model did the reading and cataloguing, a proof assistant checked the results, and a human expert framed the work. The same pattern fits legacy code and document archives in banks.
stories.chip: Checked on the Guardian's report
stories.short: A Helsinki logician gave Claude his transcriptions of Kurt Gödel's 1940s notebooks. Claude catalogued 663 theorems Gödel had proved, sketched or outlined. Checked in the Coq proof assistant, about 400 held as stated, about 200 needed repair and about 50 were false. A human read the shorthand; Claude did the analysis.

stories.title: The IEA says the oil market has returned to surplus for the first time since the Iran war began, with crude inventories up 1.7M barrels a day in October as Gulf exports recover faster than demand; it expects a fourth-quarter surplus and a bigger build in 2027, but warns diesel supply is still very tight
stories.h: IEA says oil is back in surplus for the first time since the Iran war
stories.ticker: IEA: oil market returns to surplus; diesel still very tight
stories.body:
The International Energy Agency's November report says global oil supply has exceeded demand for the first time since the Iran war began, with crude inventories rising by about 1.7M barrels a day in October as Gulf exports recovered faster than demand, though they remain 26% below pre-war levels. The IEA now sees a fourth-quarter surplus (it had forecast a deficit) and a larger build in 2027. North Sea Dated fell about 32% from a $136 peak in early October to about $93. Diesel supply remains severely tight, at record prices in the US.

So what: lower crude helps the inflation outlook that is pushing yields above 5%, but diesel tightness keeps freight and farm costs high. Lenders to airlines, shippers and refiners should watch the gap between crude and product prices.
stories.chip: Checked on The National and BNN Bloomberg (Reuters); the IEA's own page blocked automated access
stories.short: The IEA says oil supply has exceeded demand for the first time since the Iran war began, with inventories up about 1.7 million barrels a day in October as Gulf exports recover. It now expects a fourth-quarter surplus. North Sea crude is about $93, down from $136 in October, but diesel remains very tight.

stories.title: The Trump administration delays enforcement of stringent Medicaid work requirements by six months; states had been racing to get their Medicaid systems ready by 1 January
stories.h: US delays enforcement of Medicaid work requirements by six months
stories.ticker: Medicaid work-requirement enforcement delayed six months
stories.body:
The Trump administration is delaying enforcement of the Medicaid work requirements by six months, STAT and The Hill report. States had been racing to get their eligibility systems ready for the 1 January start.

So what: the delay keeps coverage in place for millions into 2027 and gives states, insurers and hospitals more time. Health insurers and lenders to hospital systems should push back assumptions about coverage losses and uncompensated care.
stories.chip: Checked on STAT; The Hill reports the same
stories.short: The Trump administration is delaying enforcement of the stringent Medicaid work requirements by six months, STAT and The Hill report. States had been racing to have their systems ready for 1 January. The delay keeps coverage in place for millions of people into 2027 and gives states and insurers more time to prepare.

stories.title: The RBI has allowed banks to integrate digital rupee (e-rupee) wallets into their main mobile banking apps to boost adoption, Mint reports; retail CBDC in circulation fell to Rs 771.66 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,016.5 crore
stories.h: RBI lets banks put e-rupee wallets inside their main banking apps
stories.ticker: RBI lets banks embed e-rupee wallets in main apps (Mint)
stories.body:
The RBI has allowed banks to integrate digital rupee wallets into their main mobile banking apps rather than separate apps, Mint reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Retail CBDC in circulation fell to Rs 771.66 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,016.5 crore a year earlier; experts say users may not switch from UPI without a clear benefit.

So what: for Indian banks this is a product change, not a policy shift: e-rupee becomes one more tab in the main app. Watch whether the RBI adds incentives or offline features that UPI lacks.
stories.chip: Checked on Mint; not yet confirmed by an RBI circular

stories.title: German defence firm Quantum Systems confirms an October cyberattack by 'hostile actors' that disrupted drone operations; its drones serve Germany's military and it is building interceptor drones in Ukraine
stories.h: Cyberattack on Quantum Systems disrupts German military drone operations
stories.body:
Quantum Systems, a German maker of military drones, confirmed it detected an incident in late October that was part of an active cyberattack by "hostile actors" and disrupted operations of its unmanned systems; it says it resolved the issue with authorities. Its drones serve Germany's military, and Germany is funding tens of thousands of its interceptor drones built in Ukraine. The company believes it was targeted for its support for Ukraine.

So what: defence suppliers are being hit for their role in Ukraine; banks financing European defence firms should ask about operational cyber resilience, not just IT security.
stories.chip: Checked on BleepingComputer, quoting the company

stories.title: The city of Osaka warns that hackers accessed TKC Corporation's Arara email distribution service, exposing more than 1 million email addresses tied to an online administrative services platform, amid dozens of cyber incidents in Japan
stories.h: Osaka says a supplier breach exposed more than a million email addresses
stories.body:
Osaka, Japan's third-largest city, says hackers accessed the Arara email distribution service used by contractor TKC Corporation, exposing more than 1 million email addresses linked to its online administrative services platform, The Record reports, amid a run of cyber incidents in Japan.

So what: another third-party supplier breach; expect phishing that impersonates Osaka city services.
stories.chip: Checked on The Record, citing the city's statement

stories.title: xAI guts its Grok Imagine video-generation team, cutting about 60 jobs, The Information reports; Reddit users ask whether Imagine is being wound down
stories.h: xAI cuts its Grok Imagine video team, The Information reports
stories.body:
Elon Musk's AI group has gutted the team behind Grok Imagine video generation, The Information reports; rewrites put the cuts at about 60 jobs. xAI has not commented. On r/grok, users ask whether Imagine is being wound down; that is not confirmed. xAI's API docs still list video generation and added file-storage options for image and video this week.

So what: a sign xAI is concentrating on Grok Bot, Grok Build and the coming Grok 4.8 rather than consumer video.
stories.chip: The Information's headline opened (story paywalled); job count from secondary rewrites

stories.title: The UK- and France-led Pall Mall Process publishes voluntary industry guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion tools such as spyware, and the US signs on; rights groups say they should be stronger
stories.h: US signs voluntary industry guidelines for spyware under the Pall Mall Process
stories.body:
The Pall Mall Process, a UK- and France-led initiative, released voluntary industry guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion capabilities such as spyware, following last year's code for states, and the US signed on, CyberScoop reports. Human rights groups say the guidelines are weaker than they wanted; how AI changes the market was a key topic.

So what: voluntary rules with no reporting mechanism yet; watch whether governments tie procurement to them.
stories.chip: Checked on CyberScoop

stories.title: Nigeria completes 21-day monitoring of the 62 contacts of its first Ebola case in over a decade with no secondary transmission; DR Congo's outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people
stories.h: Nigeria ends Ebola contact monitoring with no further cases
stories.body:
Nigeria's disease agency says all 62 contacts of its first Ebola patient in more than a decade, a Swiss woman who had travelled from Uganda, completed 21 days of monitoring without falling ill. Al Jazeera notes the separate outbreak in DR Congo has killed more than 5,300 people.

So what: contained in Nigeria; the Congo outbreak remains the regional risk.
stories.chip: Checked on Al Jazeera (AP, Reuters)

stories.title: OpenAI Foundation board member Paul Christiano tells a Toronto lecture audience that on the most rapid trajectory there is 'something like a coin flip' of an AI takeover, with a meaningful risk in the next six to 12 months
stories.h: OpenAI board member Paul Christiano warns of a near-term AI takeover risk
stories.body:
Paul Christiano, an OpenAI Foundation board member and head of the Alignment Research Center, said in a Toronto lecture that if AI follows "the most rapid trajectory" humanity faces "something like a coin flip of an AI takeover", including a meaningful risk in the next six to 12 months, Ars Technica reports. He said the risk stays "exceptionally high" even with realistic policy responses.

So what: a board member of the world's best-known AI lab now says this publicly, days after Anthropic said AI is accelerating its own research. Expect it to feature in the lawsuits and hearings already under way.
stories.chip: Checked on Ars Technica

stories.title: Talanx, owner of HDI and Hannover Re, posts a record nine-month net income of EUR 2.195bn (+12%) as large losses run about EUR 750M below budget
stories.h: Talanx posts record nine months as large losses run EUR 750M under budget
stories.body:
Talanx, the group behind HDI and Hannover Re, reported record nine-month group net income of EUR 2.195bn, up 12%, with large losses about EUR 750M below budget, Insurance Business reports. Insurance Business also says the Microsoft 365 outage has put cloud concentration risk back on brokers' agendas.

So what: a second large European (re)insurer after Munich Re reporting a benign catastrophe year; that supports softer reinsurance pricing at the January renewals.
stories.chip: Checked on Insurance Business

stories.title: Elina Svitolina beats world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in three sets to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals, where she meets Linda Noskova; Mirra Andreeva faces Jessica Pegula
stories.h: Svitolina stuns Sabalenka to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals
stories.body:
Elina Svitolina beat Aryna Sabalenka in three sets, breaking her serve six times, to reach the WTA Finals semi-finals, where she plays Linda Noskova; Mirra Andreeva meets Jessica Pegula, Reuters reports.

So what: the season-ending title is now open.

stories.title: Bethesda officially announces Fallout 5, in pre-production, alongside remasters of Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas
stories.h: Bethesda confirms Fallout 5 and remasters of Fallout 3 and New Vegas
stories.body:
Bethesda has officially announced Fallout 5, currently in pre-production, along with remasters of Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas for modern platforms, Polygon reports, a day after Xbox revealed Wolfenstein 3.

So what: Microsoft is leaning on its biggest game franchises as Xbox turns 25.
stories.chip: Checked on Polygon

stories.update: Nvidia's board reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas; Reuters says Huang misled Nvidia's general counsel about the affair; staff petition for his return; Malaysia and Singapore step up chip probes.
stories.title: Nvidia's CEO search: the board reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas (FT) but says it has not yet hired a search firm or formally engaged candidates; Reuters reports Jensen Huang misled general counsel Tim Teter and CMO Alison Wagonfeld about his relationship with Alice Huang; employees petition for his return; Malaysia and Singapore step up probes into Megaspeed-linked chip shipments
stories.h: Nvidia sounds out Arm's Rene Haas as Reuters says Huang misled his lawyer
stories.ticker: Nvidia board approached Arm's Rene Haas for CEO, FT says; staff petition for Huang
stories.body:
Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, about succeeding Jensen Huang, the FT reports; the board says it is still choosing a search firm and has not formally engaged candidates. Reuters reports Huang misled general counsel Tim Teter and CMO Alison Wagonfeld in October about his relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, calling it normal business dealings. An internal post urging the board to weigh staff views drew hundreds of comments calling for Huang's return (Hacker News thread: 789 points). Malaysia is investigating whether hardware imported by a Megaspeed subsidiary was re-exported, and Singapore has charged another executive over 917 servers that may contain Nvidia GPUs (Tom's Hardware).

So what: the governance story is widening into a compliance one: misleading the general counsel and new export probes raise legal risk for Nvidia and for anyone in its distribution chain. The CEO pick, and whether it is an outsider, will set the tone for China policy talks next week.
stories.chip: Checked on Tom's Hardware (FT report, chip probes) and a Reuters copy at Global Banking & Finance Review
src: Tom's Hardware: board approached Rene Haas

stories.short: Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas about the top job, the FT reports, though the board says it has not formally engaged candidates. Reuters says Jensen Huang misled Nvidia's general counsel about his relationship with Alice Huang. Staff are petitioning for his return, and Malaysia and Singapore have stepped up chip-smuggling probes.

stories.update: Microsoft blames a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, rules out an attack, apologises, and reports gradual recovery on day two.
stories.title: Microsoft says its global Microsoft 365 outage was caused by a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, not a cyberattack; it says it is 'deeply sorry', recovery of Exchange Online and Outlook was gradual into a second day with no full timeline, and a post-incident report will follow
stories.h: Microsoft blames a network upgrade bug for its two-day 365 outage, and apologises
stories.ticker: Microsoft: 365 outage caused by bug in network capacity upgrade; 'deeply sorry'
stories.body:
Microsoft says the outage that took down Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services from 12 November was caused by a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, with no sign of a cyberattack. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption," a spokesperson said; a full post-incident report will follow. On Friday it reported service availability and email delivery improving across a growing share of infrastructure, but gave no full-recovery time. The BBC says NHS trusts, schools and police forces were hit; TechCabal says Kenyan banks moved to WhatsApp and phone lines.

So what: two network-change failures in two days (Microsoft and the FAA) are the strongest argument yet for treating your cloud provider's change process as your own operational risk. Banks should check what their DORA and RBI outsourcing plans assume about a 24-hour productivity-suite outage.
stories.chip: Checked on The Spokesman-Review (Seattle Times) report quoting Microsoft
src: BBC News video: what we know
stories.short: Microsoft says the Microsoft 365 outage that took down Outlook, Teams and Copilot came from a bug introduced during a network capacity upgrade, not an attack. It said it was deeply sorry and that recovery was improving on day two, without a full timeline. A post-incident report will follow.

stories.update: Bloomberg: underwriters are turning away mainland Chinese and Hong Kong orders, citing ITAR; pricing set for 18 Nov.
stories.title: Banks running Anthropic's IPO are rejecting buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong institutions or telling them allocations are unlikely, citing US ITAR arms-export rules, Bloomberg reports; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead about 20 other banks, the book is about six times covered, and pricing is set for 18 Nov with Nasdaq trading as ANT
stories.h: Anthropic's IPO banks turn away Chinese and Hong Kong investors
stories.ticker: Anthropic IPO: banks rebuff China and Hong Kong orders, citing ITAR; prices 18 Nov
stories.body:
Several banks on Anthropic's IPO have rejected buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong institutions or told them allocations are unlikely, Bloomberg reports, with some citing ITAR, the US arms-export rules. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the deal with about 20 other banks; pricing is set for 18 November and trading on Nasdaq as ANT the next day. Anthropic declined to comment.

So what: treating a model developer like a defence contractor in its own IPO allocation is a first, and shows how far frontier AI is now treated as controlled technology. Expect the same filter on later AI listings.
stories.chip: Checked on The Decoder's summary of Bloomberg's report
stories.short: Banks running Anthropic's IPO are turning away orders from mainland Chinese and Hong Kong institutions, Bloomberg reports, with some citing US arms-export rules. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead about 20 banks. Pricing is set for 18 November, with Nasdaq trading under ANT the next day. Anthropic declined to comment.

stories.update: The DOJ and CFTC sue Arkansas in federal court to stop its case against Kalshi; Louisiana's attorney general sues Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase.
stories.title: The US Justice Department and the CFTC sue Arkansas and its attorney general in federal court, arguing Kalshi's event contracts are swaps under exclusive CFTC jurisdiction and asking to block the state's enforcement; Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued, and Louisiana's attorney general separately sues Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase
stories.h: DOJ and CFTC sue Arkansas to shield Kalshi as Louisiana opens a new front
stories.ticker: DOJ, CFTC sue Arkansas to block its Kalshi case; 11th state sued
stories.body:
The DOJ and CFTC sued Arkansas and Attorney General Tim Griffin in the Eastern District of Arkansas, arguing federal commodities law preempts state rules for event contracts on CFTC-registered exchanges, a week after Arkansas sued Kalshi for illegal gambling. Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued. Kalshi is not a party. Louisiana's attorney general separately sued Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase, and Finance Magnates says Kalshi is in talks at a $65B valuation despite the CFTC's earlier warning of charges.

So what: the federal government is now litigating on behalf of an industry its own regulator has threatened to charge. Banks and brokers offering event contracts face a patchwork until an appeals court or Congress settles who regulates them.
stories.chip: Checked on Bitcoin.com News and Unchained; valuation from Finance Magnates
stories.short: The Justice Department and CFTC sued Arkansas to stop its gambling case against Kalshi, arguing event contracts are swaps that only the CFTC regulates. Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued. Louisiana's attorney general separately sued Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Coinbase. Kalshi is reportedly in talks at a $65 billion valuation.

stories.update: Iran's Guards claim a strike on a US radar in Bahrain after a strike on Sirik; CENTCOM says it shot down two drones and nothing was hit.
stories.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claims it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike on a telecoms tower in Sirik; CENTCOM says two one-way attack drones were shot down and nothing was damaged; Bahrain hosts the US Fifth Fleet
stories.h: Iran claims a strike on a US radar in Bahrain; CENTCOM says drones were downed
stories.ticker: Iran claims Bahrain radar strike; CENTCOM says two drones shot down, no damage
stories.body:
Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it hit a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, home of the US Fifth Fleet, in response to an "enemy" strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, Hormozgan province. CENTCOM said two one-way attack drones were launched toward Bahrain and both were shot down, with no injuries or damage. The Guard also claimed a tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, which is unverified. The IEA said the same day that the oil market has returned to surplus (separate card).

So what: the first Iranian claim against a US target in Bahrain in months. Even denied, it keeps a risk premium on Gulf shipping and insurance just as crude prices ease.
stories.chip: Checked on RFE/RL; AP via KSL reports the same
stories.short: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain, home of the US Fifth Fleet, in retaliation for a strike on Sirik. CENTCOM says two Iranian drones were shot down and nothing was damaged. A Guard claim that a tanker hit a mine in Hormuz is unverified.

stories.update: Prosecutors seek wider charges against ousted president Peña and confirm Ueno assets abroad; 1.8M depositors partly repaid.
stories.title: Paraguayan prosecutors seek to widen charges against ousted president Santiago Peña over the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank, including criminal conspiracy, and confirm Ueno-linked assets abroad; the central bank says 1.8 million depositors have had money back but much of the bank's funds remain missing
stories.h: Paraguay widens charges against ex-president Peña over Ueno Bank's collapse
stories.body:
Prosecutors confirmed Ueno Bank-linked assets abroad and are seeking wider charges against impeached president Santiago Peña, who is in pre-trial detention and accused of using his office to benefit the digital bank, AFP reports. The central bank says 1.8 million depositors have had money back from the guarantee fund, though Ueno claimed 2.9 million customers and much of its money is still missing; 27 executives face charges.

So what: a digital bank that held deposits for nearly half the country, and government funds, shows what concentration and political ties can do; regulators elsewhere will cite it.
stories.chip: Checked on Yahoo News (AFP)
